course_description:
The course will provide students with the mathematical foundation in linear algebra and multivariable calculus needed for advanced statistical methods, data modelling, and the analysis of large data sets. Course topics are drawn primarily from linear algebra, with supporting concepts from multivariable calculus. Course content includes vectors and matrices, Gaussian elimination, determinants, orthogonal matrices, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, diagonalisation, least squares methods, singular value decomposition, covariance matrices, joint probability distributions, multivariate Gaussian distributions, Hessian matrices, clustering methods, and principal component analysis (PCA).

The ability to collect, interpret, and analyse large data sets is an important skill in making informed decisions on things including efficiency of business activities, developing trends, and making predictions, among many more. In order to develop these skills, a good understanding of various mathematical techniques and a means of carrying out these methods on a computer are imperative. This course introduces students to the basic mathematical tools and methods which will provide important background for understanding the mathematics involved in data science and practice in calculating associated quantities. Further information is on the course website: Blackboard.

course_aims:
This is a linear algebra foundations course focusing on data-science applications. There is also some emphasis on numerical computation via software. It also contains a few basic elements of multi-variable calculus and continuous optimization. At the end of the course students will possess mathematical foundations allowing understanding of several algorithms in data science.

See Blackboard for further details.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand how to apply logic to formulate a valid argument and to construct a simple proof
Gain knowledge of particular aspects of multi-variable calculus such as gradients
Be competent in extracting information from data sets by indexing and using mathematical software
Understand how matrices are used in solving systems of equations
Understand the concept of invertibility for matrices, know many criteria for invertibility and be able to find inverses
Learn how linear algebra and multi-variable calculus is applied in data scientific algorithms and methods
Gain experience in transferring mathematical ideas back and forth from computer code for problem solving
